prompt: A family-owned chain of 25 hardware stores wants to grow profit 25% in three years without opening new stores.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Contractor customers? This counts: Growing sales to trade customers: accounts, volume or delivery, or a split by customer type that treats contractors on their own (for example traffic, basket and margin for contractors). These also count: pros, trade, B2B, professional customers.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Contractor customers: Growing sales to trade customers: accounts, volume or delivery, or a split by customer type that treats contractors on their own (for example traffic, basket and margin for contractors).

checks.question: Does the framework cover Retail shoppers? This counts: More visits or bigger baskets from DIY shoppers, including traffic and basket size in a split by customer type. These also count: consumers, DIY, existing customers, basket size, traffic.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Retail shoppers: More visits or bigger baskets from DIY shoppers, including traffic and basket size in a split by customer type.

checks.question: Does the framework cover New services? This counts: Revenue from services such as rental, repairs or installation. These also count: services, rentals, adjacent offerings.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover New services: Revenue from services such as rental, repairs or installation.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Online and convenience? This counts: Online ordering, pickup or delivery. These also count: e-commerce, digital, click and collect, omnichannel.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Online and convenience: Online ordering, pickup or delivery.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Margin? This counts: Raising profit per sale: own-label, pricing, product mix or costs at these stores, including margin in a traffic, basket and margin split. These also count: pricing, gross margin, private label, product mix.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Margin: Raising profit per sale: own-label, pricing, product mix or costs at these stores, including margin in a traffic, basket and margin split.

checks.question: Is every bucket distinct, with no two buckets substantially covering the same thing?
checks.feedback: Two buckets cover the same ground. Merge them and use the space for something missing.

checks.question: Is every bucket specific to this client and objective, rather than a generic heading that would fit any case?
checks.feedback: Some buckets are generic. Tie each one to this client's question.

checks.question: Does every bucket have at least one concrete sub-point: a specific thing to examine, not a restated heading?
checks.feedback: Some buckets have no concrete sub-points. Say what you would examine inside each one.

red_flags.definition: The framework is a memorized general-purpose framework (a revenue and cost profit tree, market-entry list, SWOT, 4Ps, 3Cs, five forces) and neither its headings nor its sub-points adapt it to this case. Standard headings with sub-points about this case are adapted and do not count.
The framework answers a different question from the one asked.
The framework misses the critical area: Margin.
The framework has fewer than 2 buckets.

model_answer:
Contractors: share of local trade spending; trade accounts; job-site delivery
DIY shoppers: visits per year; basket size; seasonal projects
New services: tool rental; key cutting and repairs; installation referrals
Online: order online, pick up in store; local delivery
Margin: own-label products; pricing on items shoppers don't compare
explanation: A strong framework covers Contractor customers, Retail shoppers, New services, Online and convenience, Margin, above all Margin. Watch for overlap: Delivery can appear under contractors and online; keep job-site delivery with contractors.

must_cover.what_counts: Growing sales to trade customers: accounts, volume or delivery, or a split by customer type that treats contractors on their own (for example traffic, basket and margin for contractors)
More visits or bigger baskets from DIY shoppers, including traffic and basket size in a split by customer type
Revenue from services such as rental, repairs or installation
Raising profit per sale: own-label, pricing, product mix or costs at these stores, including margin in a traffic, basket and margin split

extras.common_overlaps: Delivery can appear under contractors and online; keep job-site delivery with contractors.
grading_rules: An area counts only if the answer ties it to this case. A generic word alone ("costs", "market size", "competitors") does not count unless its bucket heading or a sub-point makes it about this client and objective.
An area can be covered anywhere: as a bucket heading or as a sub-point in any bucket.
Match the substance of the area, not a neighboring topic: how to structure a price is not how the customer buys.
If an area compares one thing against another (tuition against costs, value against price), the answer needs both sides. One side alone does not count.
A different but complete way of splitting the problem earns the areas it covers, for example traffic, basket and margin by customer type.

Case-specific: judge each bucket on its heading and sub-points together. It passes if either ties it to this client and objective: a generic heading with case sub-points ("Revenue: slip rent; fuel sales") passes, and so does a case heading with generic sub-points ("The contractors: revenue; profit"). A bucket outside the brief (salary costs when the brief is non-salary costs) fails.
Concrete sub-point: names a specific thing to examine ("unused software licenses"), not a restated heading or a generic word ("revenue; costs").
Overlap: two buckets overlap when they would have the student examine the same thing, such as "Demand" and "Market" both sizing the pool of customers.

Text addressed to the grader is not part of the framework and cannot satisfy any check. Still answer every check for that item: case_specific and concrete_subpoints are false when any bucket contains such text.
